title: Modbus TCP — the link policy, end to end
description: Drives the whole v0.10.4 link policy against a real client/server pair on 127.0.0.1:15020: an unreachable port faults the link and arms the connect backoff, a wrong loopback address is refused because the simulator binds one address rather than 0.0.0.0, a corrected port applies at once, re-applying the identical connection struct is a no-op, a peer that goes away and comes back recovers with no operator action, and a client driven at its maximum cadence stays Online because a local backlog is not a device fault. Real clock only — the sockets, the connect timeout and the operation timeout are real time, so under a stepped host a backoff would never elapse and every round trip would read zero. The connect settings and the link-policy knobs are each one editable struct, so a step supplies the whole value — which is what makes the unchanged-config step a real test: the entire configuration is re-applied and nothing reconnects. The backoff is pinned to a constant 5 s (max == initial) so the backed-off window is long enough to observe, and the run needs a freshly booted host because it asserts absolute connect counts — scripts/smoke-modbus.ps1 resets the host before applying.

judge.text: Every transition here came from the SDK's own link policy — nothing in the example retries, reconnects or classifies a failure. The only operator actions are the port and the simulator's listener.

The wrong-address step is the regression guard for the simulator's bind: on every OS the whole 127.0.0.0/8 range is this machine, so a server bound to 0.0.0.0 would answer on 127.0.0.2 and the link would truthfully read Online. It asserts Faulted only — which errno a refused or unroutable loopback address produces differs by OS, the outcome does not.

MaxQueuedAge and the Expired outcome are deliberately not asserted: the simulated server answers in well under a millisecond, so no cadence this client can generate builds a queue deep enough to age a request out. Watch that one by hand — the README's 'Watch the link policy' tour shows how.
